57: // trim removes all failure, warning, success or skipped results that depend on
58: // a result reported as failure, warning or skipped. Dependencies are declared
59: // by setting the metadata via metadataDependsOn.
60: func trim(results *[]Outcome) {
61: 	// holds codes for all failures, warnings or skipped rules, as a map to ease
62: 	// the lookup, any rule that depends on a reported code will be removed from
63: 	// the results
64: 	reported := map[string]bool{}
65: 
66: 	for _, checks := range *results {
67: 		for _, results := range [][]Result{checks.Failures, checks.Warnings, checks.Skipped} {
68: 			for _, result := range results {
69: 				if code, ok := result.Metadata[metadataCode].(string); ok {
70: 					reported[code] = true
71: 				}
72: 			}
73: 		}
74: 	}
75: 
76: 	// helper function inlined for ecapsulation, removes any results that depend
77: 	// on a reported rule, by code
78: 	trimOutput := func(what []Result) []Result {
79: 		if what == nil {
80: 			// nil might get passed in, while this would not cause an issue, the
81: 			// function would return empty array and that would needlessly
82: 			// change the output
83: 			return nil
84: 		}
85: 
86: 		// holds leftover results, i.e. the ones that do not depend on a rule
87: 		// reported as failure, warning or skipped
88: 		trimmed := make([]Result, 0, len(what))
89: 		for _, result := range what {
90: 			if dependency, ok := result.Metadata[metadataDependsOn].([]string); ok {
91: 				for _, d := range dependency {
92: 					if !reported[d] {
93: 						trimmed = append(trimmed, result)
94: 					}

108: 			if description, ok = results[i].Metadata[metadataDescription].(string); !ok {

This release contains a mix of features, performance improvements, and bugfixes.

### Optimized read mode for OPA's in-memory store ([#7125](https://github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/pull/7125))

A new optimized read mode has been added to the default in-memory store, where data written to the store is eagerly converted  
to AST values (the data format used during evaluation). This removes the time spent converting raw data values to AST  
during policy evaluation, thereby improving performance.

The memory footprint of the store will increase, as processed AST values generally take up more space in memory than the  
corresponding raw data values, but overall memory usage of OPA might remain more stable over time, as pre-converted data  
is shared across evaluations and isn't recomputed for each evaluation, which can cause spikes in memory usage.

This mode can be enabled for `opa run`, `opa eval`, and `opa bench` by setting the `--optimize-store-for-read-speed` flag.

More information about this feature can be found [here](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/v0.70.0/policy-performance/#storage-optimization).

Co-authored by [@johanfylling](https://github.com/johanfylling) and [@ashutosh-narkar](https://github.com/ashutosh-narkar).
